import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Specifications Analysis (n=1000)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Plot 1: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sensor_types = df['sensor_type'].unique()
colors = sns.color_palette('husl', len(sensor_types))
for sensor, color in zip(sensor_types, colors):
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], alpha=0.6, label=sensor, c=[color], s=30)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', fontsize=8, title_fontsize=9, loc='upper left')
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Average Price by Brand (Top 10 brands)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
brand_stats = df.groupby('brand').agg({'price_usd': 'mean', 'brand': 'count'}).rename(columns={'brand': 'count'})
brand_stats = brand_stats.sort_values('price_usd', ascending=True).tail(10)
bars = ax2.barh(brand_stats.index, brand_stats['price_usd'], color=sns.color_palette('viridis', 10))
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Top 10 Brands by Average Price', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')
for i, (bar, price) in enumerate(zip(bars, brand_stats['price_usd'])):
    ax2.text(price + 50, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'${price:.0f}', va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 3: Distribution of Cameras by Body Type and 4K Video Capability
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.columns = ['No 4K', 'Has 4K']
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color=['#ff7f0e', '#1f77b4'], edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Camera Distribution by Body Type and 4K Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(title='4K Video', fontsize=9, title_fontsize=10)
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 4: Weight vs Max ISO by Body Type
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
markers = ['o', 's', '^', 'D', 'v']
colors_body = sns.color_palette('Set2', len(body_types))
for body, color, marker in zip(body_types, colors_body, markers):
    subset = df[df['body_type'] == body]
    ax4.scatter(subset['weight_grams'], subset['max_iso'], alpha=0.6, label=body, 
                c=[color], s=40, marker=marker)
ax4.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Max ISO', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Weight vs Max ISO by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(title='Body Type', fontsize=9, title_fontsize=10)
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax4.set_yscale('log')

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
